title: Anti-COVID-measures and vaccine-mandate demonstration in central Vienna
location: Heldenplatz and Maria-Theresien-Platz, procession along Vienna Ringstraße, ending at Heldenplatz
organizer: Not established by the contemporaneous report
participants_original: Police estimated around 40,000; organizers claimed a substantially larger, unquantified number.
threshold_50_evidence: ORF Wien attributes an estimate of around 40,000 assembled demonstrators to police; organizers claimed more. The explicit police estimate is well above 50.

occurrence.summary: ORF reports the Saturday gathering and march in the past tense, including its route and return to Heldenplatz.

start_date.summary: Article gives the event date as 8 January 2022.

location.summary: Participants assembled at Heldenplatz and Maria-Theresien-Platz, moved along the Ring and returned to Heldenplatz.

demands.summary: The article says protesters opposed COVID measures and quotes signs opposing compulsory vaccination.

participants_original.summary: Police estimated about 40,000; organizers claimed a much larger number without quantifying it.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The police estimate of about 40,000 is an explicit crowd estimate far above the 50-person threshold.

protester_violence.summary: The report says some people tried forcibly to breach a police barrier; this supports yes for violence during the protest.

state_response.summary: Police used pepper spray to stop the attempted breach and reported four arrests; other response dimensions are not reported.

notes: ORF says some demonstrators attempted to force through a police barrier; police used pepper spray and arrested four. This is an individual gathering dated Jan. 8; linkage to a broader weekly campaign is unresolved. The closing rally’s exact end time is not established even though the Ring was largely reopened around 18:30.
open_questions: How does this dated gathering relate to the recurring anti-COVID-measures demonstrations before and after January?
Does later reporting establish the physical end of this event or only a last reported point of activity?

threshold_50_evidence: ORF Tirol attributes a crowd of about 6,000 to police.

start_date.summary: Article dates the gathering to 9 January 2022.

location.summary: The crowd assembled at Landhausplatz and later marched through the city centre.

organizer.summary: The article names Team Tirol as event organizer and says FPÖ, MFG and Team Tirol jointly called the larger demonstration.

demands.summary: The event was explicitly against the federal government’s COVID measures and vaccine mandate.

participants_original.summary: ORF body attributes about 6,000 to police; the Ministry answer has one Innsbruck row for 9 Jan, approx. 6,000 (physical PDF p.18). Likely match by date/place/estimate; official source does not identify the specific assembly or count origin.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: ORF police estimate of about 6,000 is well above 50.

notes: Separate from the antifascist counter-demonstration of 80 at Walther-Park, which is excluded for lack of a reported domestic state/policy demand. This is a distinct Sunday action; exact link to the recurring demonstration campaign remains open. Ministry table row on physical p.18 matches the same date, place and approximate headcount; it likely reports the same police estimate, so is not counted as independent corroboration.
open_questions: How does this dated gathering relate to the recurring anti-COVID-measures demonstrations before and after January?
Does later reporting establish the physical end of this event or only a last reported point of activity?

title: Anti-COVID-measures and vaccine-mandate demonstration in central Vienna
location: Heldenplatz, area around Votivkirche and procession over the Vienna Ring
organizer: FPÖ officials including Herbert Kickl spoke; no formal event organizer established in report
participants_original: Police estimate about 27,000; another passage in the same ORF article says around 30,000.
threshold_50_evidence: ORF Wien gives a police estimate of about 27,000 in the lead and main report; a later repeated passage says around 30,000. The lower stated estimate is used for the count and clearly exceeds 50.

occurrence.summary: ORF and Reuters/Euronews separately report the Vienna protest on 15 January; Reuters calls the Saturday action a routine event.

start_date.summary: Article explicitly dates the rally to 15 January 2022.

location.summary: The report names Heldenplatz, the Votivkirche area and the Ring route.

demands.summary: ORF reports opposition to COVID measures and the vaccine mandate; Reuters/Euronews identifies the target as government plans for mandatory COVID vaccination and a government-resignation chant.

participants_original.summary: Police estimate about 27,000; a repeated page passage says around 30,000.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The lower explicit police estimate of 27,000 is well above 50.

state_response.summary: Police reported arrests and mask-rule enforcement; event-level beating, shootings, killings and accommodation are not established.

notes: ORF’s two attendance formulations are not independent sources; retain 27,000 as the lower explicit estimate. The article reports the demonstration continued at least six hours after it began, but does not establish the physical ending. The exact weekly-campaign onset and event linkage are unresolved. Reuters/Euronews S023 independently confirms a 15 Jan Vienna anti-mandate demonstration and routine Saturday context, but says only “thousands”; it does not corroborate the 27,000 figure.
open_questions: How does this dated gathering relate to the recurring anti-COVID-measures demonstrations before and after January?
Does later reporting establish the physical end of this event or only a last reported point of activity?

title: Anti-vaccine-mandate demonstrations during the National Council vote in Vienna
location: Central Vienna; an approximately 150-person demonstration at Josefsplatz and other separately reported assemblies near the Hofburg, Volksgarten and Mariahilfer Straße
scope: Local; several central-Vienna gatherings on the same day. Whether the Hofburg/Volksgarten/Mariahilfer action is the same organized demonstration or a distinct one is unresolved.
participants_original: ORF says approximately 150 at the Josefsplatz demonstration and up to 500 across Thursday’s several demonstrations; the second report says nearly 200 across its described locations.
threshold_50_evidence: ORF police reporting attributes about 150 people to a specific Josefsplatz demonstration, which by itself exceeds 50; broader same-day event boundaries and counts remain unresolved.

occurrence.summary: ORF reports multiple anti-mandate demonstrations in central Vienna during the National Council vote on 20 January.

start_date.summary: Both reports describe demonstrations taking place on 20 January 2022.

location.summary: Reports place gatherings near the Hofburg, Volksgarten, Maria-Theresien-Platz, Mariahilfer Straße and Josefsplatz; whether they form one event remains unresolved.

demands.summary: Demonstrators protested the National Council’s adoption of the COVID vaccine mandate and criticized COVID measures.

participants_original.summary: Police reported about 150 at the Josefsplatz demonstration and up to 500 across the several Thursday demonstrations; S004 separately says nearly 200 across its reported gathering/route.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The police report gives approximately 150 at one named Josefsplatz demonstration, sufficient to clear 50.

state_response.summary: Police dissolved the Josefsplatz demonstration; aggregate arrests and citations are reported for the day but are not allocated to this specific gathering.

notes: Do not add the approximately 150 Josefsplatz estimate to the up-to-500 across all Thursday demonstrations. The article says six arrests and a dissolution occurred across the day’s demonstrations but does not assign all response actions to this specific gathering. Hold event-level ownership and exact event unit for review; the policy target and qualifying crowd are documented.
open_questions: How does this dated gathering relate to the recurring anti-COVID-measures demonstrations before and after January?
Does later reporting establish the physical end of this event or only a last reported point of activity?

title: Anti-vaccine-mandate demonstration in Linz
location: Route through Linz along Landstraße and Wiener Straße, then back toward the city centre
participants_original: ORF reports 1,400 in the largest of several Jan. 19 Linz actions; the Ministry answer p.11 lists two Linz rows that day, approx. 20 and 1,400. The 1,400 row aligns with the reported largest march.
threshold_50_evidence: ORF Oberösterreich gives a police-reported 1,400 participants for the largest march, well above the threshold.

occurrence.summary: ORF reports multiple completed demonstrations in Linz on Wednesday 19 January; the largest march followed a specified route.

start_date.summary: Article explicitly dates the actions to 19 January 2022.

location.summary: The largest march ran along Landstraße to Wiener Straße and back.

demands.summary: Reports protests against the vaccine mandate and COVID measures; participants criticized mask requirements.

participants_original.summary: ORF attributes 1,400 to the largest march; the Ministry answer table has two 19 Jan Linz rows, 20 and 1,400 (physical PDF p.11). Date, place and attendance align with the reported largest march; the ministry does not identify the march by name.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The 1,400 police-reported participants in the largest march exceeds 50.

state_response.summary: Police recorded 21 mask-related citations plus other reports. The account of police pushing demonstrators back at the children’s facility is disputed by the police department.

notes: The article distinguishes several partly unregistered demonstrations; 1,400 applies only to the largest route. At a stop by an after-school facility, the report records participants criticizing mask rules and a disputed account of police pushing some participants back, denied by the police department. No protester violence or specific force response is inferred. Episode relation to other city/weekend anti-mandate rallies remains open. The p.11 Ministry table includes a second Linz row (approx. 20) the same day, consistent with multiple actions in S006; only the 1,400 row is matched to the reported largest march. The Ministry estimate may share police provenance with ORF.
open_questions: How does this dated gathering relate to the recurring anti-COVID-measures demonstrations before and after January?
Does later reporting establish the physical end of this event or only a last reported point of activity?

threshold_50_evidence: ORF’s approximately 1,000 attendees and the date/place-matched Ministry table entry exceed 50.

occurrence.summary: ORF reports the completed Bregenz anti-mandate march on Thursday 20 January.

start_date.summary: Article gives the event date as 20 January 2022.

location.summary: The article describes a route from the district authority via Seestraße and HTL to the Landhaus.

organizer.summary: ORF names Freie Bürger-Partei (FBP) as organizer.

demands.summary: The report identifies the demonstration as against the vaccine mandate.

participants_original.summary: ORF reports around 1,000 attendees; Ministry table p.19 records approx. 1,000 in Bregenz on 20 Jan. Likely same estimate, not independent.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The reported crowd of around 1,000 is well above 50.

state_response.summary: Police chose not to issue mask citations, saying they sought to prevent escalation; other dimensions are unreported.

notes: The Ministry row matches date, city and approximate number but has no assembly identifier. ORF’s timestamp (15:54) precedes its narrative’s 16:00 start despite past-tense attendance; keep date only and do not infer precise timing. The Ministry’s number may use the same police estimate.
open_questions: Is this distinct from the later 22 Jan Bregenz rally?
What is the verified physical end time?

title: Anti-vaccine-mandate demonstration in Graz
location: Graz city area; exact route/assembly point not specified in the reports
participants_original: ORF Steiermark reports an anti-mandate demonstration without a crowd count. Ministry table lists 13,500 for Graz city area on 22 Jan (physical p.16); likely this large row corresponds to the reported anti-mandate rally.
threshold_50_evidence: The Ministry answer has a row for Graz city area, 22 Jan, approx. 13,500 (physical p.16); ORF verifies the same-day anti-mandate gathering.

occurrence.summary: ORF Steiermark and the national ORF roundup report a Graz demonstration on 22 Jan; the national roundup overlaps with regional coverage.

start_date.summary: Both reports place the anti-mandate event on Saturday 22 January.

location.summary: Graz is identified, but the articles do not specify a precise site/route.

demands.summary: Both describe the large demonstration as against the vaccine mandate.

participants_original.summary: The visually inspected ministry table records approx. 13,500 for Graz city area on 22 Jan (physical p.16). ORF’s regional report gives no Graz count and the national roundup says only several thousand across Graz and Bregenz; matching this larger row to the anti-mandate event is an inference from the separate 200-person row and its much larger rally description.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: ORF reports a large rally and the date/city-aligned ministry row gives approx. 13,500.

protester_violence.summary: ORF reports police injured and five judicial complaints in connection with the anti-mandate demonstration; individual acts/actors are not separately assigned.

state_response.summary: Five provisional arrests and administrative/judicial complaints are reported; other response dimensions are not established.

notes: The official p.16 table contains two Graz city entries on 22 Jan, 200 and 13,500. The larger entry is matched to this anti-mandate rally by the contemporaneous reporting of a large event, while the separate smaller solidarity gathering is described below; there is no identifier tying either row to a named assembly. S010 overlaps with S008 and is not independent corroboration.
open_questions: Can a source identify which official row corresponds to which assembly?
Does the crowd-estimate discrepancy with the national roundup reflect rounding, source timing or a row/event mismatch?
What is the physical event end time and its broader episode link?

title: Separate “more solidarity” gathering in Graz
location: Graz city area; exact site/route not specified
participants_original: ORF describes attendance in the lower three digits. The official ministry table has a separate 22 Jan Graz row of approx. 200 on physical p.16, a likely but unconfirmed match.
threshold_50_evidence: ORF’s “lower three-digit” estimate establishes at least 100 attendees; the separate 200-person ministry row is a possible date/place match.

occurrence.summary: Both ORF reports distinguish a second Graz gathering from the anti-mandate demonstration.

start_date.summary: The separate gathering is reported on 22 January 2022.

location.summary: Graz city is identified; the precise site/route is not provided.

participants_original.summary: ORF describes a lower-three-digit crowd. Ministry p.16 lists a separate Graz city row of approx. 200 on 22 Jan. The match is plausible by count/date/place but not keyed to an assembly.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The contemporaneous ORF description “lower three-digit” exceeds 50.

demands.summary: Reports describe “more solidarity” and opposition to a rightward shift; they explicitly separate it from anti-mandate demonstration. They do not establish a specific demand addressed to Austrian state policy; one report also refers to pandemic mismanagement.

state_response.summary: No event-specific state response to the separate gathering is described.

notes: Do not merge this event with the Graz anti-mandate demonstration. The exact match to the 200 ministry row is inferential; the event is distinct according to ORF. “More solidarity” and opposition to a rightward shift are not alone a verified domestic state-policy target. A reference to pandemic mismanagement may imply one, but needs exact body context; target remains pending.
open_questions: What precise demands were made and were they directed to the Austrian government or its policy?
Which of the two ministry table rows corresponds to this gathering?

organizer: Twenty-two assemblies were registered; event organizer not established in the report
participants_original: Police estimated 10,000 in the afternoon march formed when individual assemblies merged.
threshold_50_evidence: The police estimate of 10,000 in the merged march exceeds 50.

location.summary: Assemblies were announced at Maria-Theresien-Platz, Heldenplatz and Schwarzenbergplatz and merged into a Ring march.

demands.summary: The article identifies the demonstrations as against COVID measures.

participants_original.summary: Police estimate of 10,000 refers to the merged march, not separately to each of the 22 registered assemblies.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The police estimate for the merged march is about 10,000.

state_response.summary: ORF reports pepper spray and arrests; other dimensions are not established.

notes: The candidate preserves the reported merged march as the observable crowd. Did pepper spray target this merged crowd and did it end the event?
